lines.text: Before anything moves, every device gets its own number.
Open the motor, and factory default it. That clears whatever last season left behind.
Click Blink. The device that flashes is the one you're editing. If two flash together, they share an ID.
Give each one its number and a name. The arm's motor is thirty one, its encoder is thirty two, and the flywheel is twenty one.
On the arm, turn it counterclockwise by hand, and the encoder's number should climb. Zero it with the arm level, and a quarter turn up reads point two five.
Then tell the arm's motor to use that encoder for its position. In the feedback settings, that's the encoder's ID, and remote CANcoder.
Now the first motion. Pick Voltage Out, and ask for one volt. It sends that voltage and nothing else. There's no target, and no place to stop.
Enable it. The mechanism moves the moment you click, and it keeps going until you click again.
Try it. Enable it, and stop it before it reaches the end.
Check the direction. The arm should turn counterclockwise, with the encoder counting up. If it goes the wrong way, invert the motor in its settings. Don't type a negative voltage.
Every device has its own number, and positive means the same thing everywhere, before any code runs.
